summary: Bratindra Nath Mukherjee was an Indologist and historian. He earned a master's at the University of Calcutta and a doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later serving as Carmichael Professor at Calcutta from 1975 to 1998.

Brendan Ozawa-de Silva specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a D.Phil. from Oxford and a Ph.D. from Emory, later serving as Associate Professor at Life University (2012–2017) and Emory University (2022).

Brendan S. Gillon works in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, he served as Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University around 1992, with affiliation attested there through 2024–2025.

Bret W. Davis is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Vanderbilt and Kyoto University, he taught at Shiga and Kwansei Gakuin Universities and held philosophy appointments at Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007, 2018).
Brian Bocking is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Michael Pye and earned his PhD from the University of Leeds (attested 1984).

Brian Cutillo was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from roughly 1963 to 1967 and studied under Geshe Wangyal between around 1971 and 1983.

Brian D. Ruppert is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Willis Stoesz. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1998–2016) and Bates College (~2016).

Brian Daizen Victoria is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Komazawa and Temple Universities, and held posts at the University of Auckland, Antioch University, and the University of Adelaide, among others.

Brian Gregory Baumann works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington under György Kara, and taught Mongolian for UC Berkeley and the Numata Center (attested 2026).

Brian Houghton Hodgson was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at East India Company College and Fort William College, he served as Assistant Resident and later British Resident in Nepal between 1820 and 1843.

Brian J. Nichols is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne Carolyn Klein and also studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies.

Bridget Allchin was a scholar of archaeology and Indology. She studied at the University of Cape Town and earned her PhD at University College London, later serving as a Fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1977–2017).
Brigitte Marschall earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna, where she later served as an extraordinary university professor around 1997.
Brigitte Steinmann is a scholar of Tibetology who studied under Alexander W. Macdonald and Bahadur Singh. She held a post at the University of Montpellier (attested 2004).

Brij Kishor Tripathi worked in Indology and Tibetology as a Research Assistant at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1995), later teaching mathematics at several engineering institutions including Lukhdhirji and L.D. College of Engineering.

Bronislav Ivanovič Kuznecov was a Tibetologist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vladimir Vorob’ëv-Desjatovskij and Boris Pankratov from ~1951 to 1956, later teaching there in 1959.

Bronisław Malinowski was an anthropologist who studied at the Jagiellonian University, Leipzig, and the London School of Economics. He held a chair in anthropology at LSE (1922–1938) and later served as professor at Yale (~1939–1942).

Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned degrees from Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland, and held faculty posts at Marquette University (2012–2014) and the Australian National University (from 2014).

Brook Ziporyn works in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Chicago and the University of Michigan, he held positions at Northwestern University (~1999–2012) and the University of Chicago, where he became Mircea Eliade Professor around 2016.

Brooke Foss Westcott was a religious studies scholar who studied at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Trinity College, Cambridge. He later held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1870 to 1890.
